questions.question: A pattern goes: red, blue, red, blue, red, blue. What is the core?
questions.explain: The core is the shortest group that repeats over and over. A common trap is stopping too early at just one colour instead of the full pair.

questions.question: A pattern goes: star, star, moon, star, star, moon, star, star, moon. What is the core?
options: star, star, moon, star, star, moon
questions.explain: The core is the group that repeats, and here it is three words: star, star, moon. A common mistake is leaving out the moon and stopping too soon.

questions.question: A pattern goes: up, down, up, down, up, down. What is the core?
questions.explain: The core is the smallest repeating group, which here is up, down. A common trap is taking two full repeats and calling them one core.

questions.question: A pattern goes: cat, dog, bird, cat, dog, bird, cat, dog, bird. What is the core?
options: cat, dog, bird, cat, dog, bird
questions.explain: The core is the full group that repeats, which here is cat, dog, bird. A common trap is stopping too early and leaving out the bird.

questions.question: A girl strings beads: red, yellow, red, yellow, red, yellow. Her teacher says every repeating pattern has a core. What is this core?
questions.explain: The core is the shortest part that repeats, and here it is red, yellow. Picking just one bead is too short for a core.

questions.question: A teacher taps a drum: tap, tap, pause, tap, tap, pause, tap, tap, pause. A boy says the core is just 'tap, tap'. What is the real core?
options: tap, tap, pause, tap, tap, pause
questions.explain: The core must include everything that repeats together, so it is tap, tap, pause. Stopping at tap, tap leaves out the pause.

questions.question: A girl draws: circle, triangle, circle, triangle, circle, triangle. She says the core is 'circle, triangle, circle, triangle'. What is the real core?
questions.explain: The core is one full repeat, not two. Circle, triangle repeats three times, so that is the correct core.

questions.question: Cups on a table go: apple, orange, apple, orange, apple, orange. A child says the core is 'apple, orange, apple, orange, apple, orange'. What is the real core?
options: apple, orange, apple, orange, apple, orange
questions.explain: The core is one repeat, not the whole row. Apple, orange repeats three times, so that is the core.

questions.question: A boy writes: star, heart, star, heart, star, heart. He says the core is 'star, heart, star, heart'. What is his mistake?
options: He used two repeats as one core
He stopped the core too short
He added a shape not in the list
He swapped the order of the shapes
questions.explain: The core is ONE repeat, not two. Star, heart repeats three times, so using two repeats makes the core too long.

questions.question: A pattern is: up, down, left, up, down, left, up, down, left. A child says the core is 'up, down'. What is wrong with that?
options: It is too long for a core
It should be one word only
questions.explain: The core must include every part that repeats together. Here, up, down, left repeats, so stopping at up, down leaves out the left.

questions.question: A pattern is: A, B, B, A, B, B, A, B, B. A girl says the core is 'A, B'. Why is that not the full core?
options: It is too long for a core
It should be one letter only
It leaves out the second B
questions.explain: The core must include all the parts that repeat together. Here the second B goes with the first B, so the core is A, B, B.

questions.question: A pattern is: big, small, small, big, small, small, big, small, small. A child says the core is 'big, small, small, big, small, small'. What is the real core?
options: big, small, small, big, small, small
questions.explain: The core is one full repeat, not two. Big, small, small repeats three times, so that is the core.
